footer: Gifford et al. 2014 Lab Chip 14, 4496-4505, Fig. 6 (adapted; © The Royal Society of Chemistry: permission for reproduction to be obtained before publication, README), with every edge of (a) the first rc6 variant of gifford2014_fig6_design and (b) the shipped rc6 preset gifford2014_fig6_design, which now takes the micrograph's layout (cyan), each on one map fitted on the ends of legs 5, 3 and 1 (scale 4.5248 µm/px from the printed 125 µm centre; rows at 49.81°).  Both take the micrograph's leg positions for legs 7, 5, 3, 1 and leg 7's early end (pc_last_short 257 µm).  (a) The generator's uniform paperclip at the micrograph's 588 µm spacing: its turns are semicircles of radius d/2 about a point one half-spacing beyond leg 1 (the generator's own rule for this device: 723 µm, radius 362 µm).  (b) The leg axes read on the micrograph (reproduction.leg_Y): the 16 turn walls of legs 5, 3, 1 are concentric arcs about one centre 1745.7 µm beyond leg 1 (residual SD 0.59 µm; the centre's SD 2.2 µm in the common fit, 26 µm between the walls fitted one by one), and semicircular turns about it put legs 2, 4, 6 at 3491, 4079, 4667 µm (2 Y_c - Y, which doubles the centre's error); only 8-23° of each turn is in the frame, so the semicircle (and legs 2, 4, 6) is an assumption.  (b) agrees with the image's turns by construction (its leg axes are read on them: consistency, not a test) except along the flow, which nothing read on the turns sets: the mask's turns start 5.7 µm downstream of the image's.  Under each panel: the nearest-outline metric of all claimed edges and, for the turns alone, the distance from each wall point followed on the image to the mask's nearest edge, and the two sets' common-centre fits (panels_gifford6.turn_compare).
